title: Claims Rulebook: Unauthorized Payments on the Pocketwire Personal Account
content:
### Coverage

An unauthorized-payment claim covers a payment sent from the Pocketwire Personal Account that the customer did not make or authorize; a payment the customer made themselves — including one sent to the wrong person, one induced by a seller who never delivered, or one sent from a shared device the customer let someone use — is not unauthorized.

### Filing

- **Report window.** The claim is accepted only within the report window: the claim is filed no later than the plan's report window in calendar days after the disputed payment's transaction date. The report window is counted in calendar days from the disputed payment's transaction date, the day after the payment being day 1, and a claim filed on the last day of the window is accepted.
- **One claim per payment.** A payment can carry only one claim of either type: a claim is filed only if no earlier claim of any type or outcome exists on the same payment, so an unauthorized claim and a purchase protection claim are mutually exclusive on one payment.
- The transaction date and any earlier claim are read from the system records of the disputed payment and of the account's claims.

| Hypothetical illustration, a 60-day report window | Accepted? |
|---|---|
| Filed on the 60th calendar day after the transaction date | Yes |
| Filed on the 61st calendar day after the transaction date | No |

### Liability

The customer's liability is computed at filing: when the claim is filed within the timely-notice period in business days after the payment's transaction date, liability is the lower of the claim amount and the plan's timely-notice liability cap; otherwise it is the lower of the claim amount and the plan's later-notice liability cap. Business days are Federal Reserve business days — Monday through Friday excluding federal holidays — and the first business day after the transaction date is day 1.

| Hypothetical claim | Notice | Cap | Liability | Claim amount less liability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 120.00 | Timely | 50.00 | 50.00 | 70.00 |
| 120.00 | Later, inside the report window | 500.00 | 120.00 | 0.00 |
| 800.00 | Later, inside the report window | 500.00 | 500.00 | 300.00 |

### Provisional credit

Provisional credit of the claim amount less the customer's liability is posted once the claim has stayed pending long enough: provisional credit is posted no earlier than the plan's provisional credit timing in business days after the claim report date, and only on a claim whose latest record is still pending. Provisional-credit timing is counted in Federal Reserve business days from the claim report date, the first business day after the report being day 1, and posting on the day the period is reached qualifies. Provisional credit is posted at most once on a disputed payment. When the disputed payment's transaction date falls within the plan's new-account period in calendar days after the account opened date, the new-account provisional credit timing replaces the standard timing, and the new-account investigation deadline in calendar days replaces the investigation deadline in business days.

### Resolution

The claims team records approved or denied; a claim still pending after the plan's investigation deadline in business days (or the new-account investigation deadline in calendar days for a new-account payment) from the report date is resolved as approved on the next handling. On approval, a provisional credit already posted becomes final with no further entry, and when none was posted the claim amount less the liability is reimbursed as a claim reimbursement. On denial, or on withdrawal by the customer, a posted provisional credit is reversed in full; the customer's withdrawal is the customer's own decision, confirmed by the customer, and ends the claim for good.

| Outcome | Provisional credit posted | Provisional credit not posted |
|---|---|---|
| Approved | Becomes final; no further entry | Claim amount less liability reimbursed |
| Denied or withdrawn | Reversed in full | Nothing to reverse |
